title: BlueGate Systems - partner discovery & evaluation framing
summary: Introductory alignment on potential partnership to offer BlueGate customers a hybrid GPU onramp that ties into Redwood's Dedicated and Private offerings; discussed integration constraints (VPC, KMS, data residency), pilot scope, and benchmarking needs.
next_steps: Redwood to share security overview + SOC2 addendum (Samir) - by 2026-07-28
BlueGate to send representative workload sample and perf targets (Ibrahim/Tomás) - by 2026-07-30
Schedule a SE deep-dive to map network topology for VPC peering (Lana + Priya) - week of 2026-08-03
action_items: Samir - send Redwood security brief, SOC2 docs, and tenant isolation options - 2026-07-28
Lana - prepare preliminary benchmark plan and list of metrics we will capture (latency p50/p95, tokens/sec) - 2026-07-31
Ibrahim - provide sample inference traffic shape (seq len distribution, batch sizes, qps) and VPC diagram - 2026-07-30
Priya - confirm KMS/HSM requirements and any regulatory constraints (data residency) - 2026-07-30
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-23 16:00 UTC | Duration ~52m
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lana Ortiz (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (BlueGate Head of Platform), Derek Voss (CTO), Ibrahim Al-Karim (Infra), Priya Rao (Security), Tomás Rivera (PM)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir from Redwood, that's Lana our solutions engineer. Quick check - is this still a good time?
[00:12] Maya: Yep good, thanks. We're excited to explore how we might bundle GPU onramp options for our enterprise customers.
[00:20] Samir: Great. High level we'll cover integration patterns - hosted API, dedicated reserved pods, and private VPC/on-prem patterns, then dig into your constraints and pilot.
[00:30] Derek: Quick ask up front - many of our customers have strict data residency and want on-prem or VPC with KMS integration. How mature are those flows?
[00:40] Lana: We're fairly mature - Redwood Private supports VPC installs and customer-managed KMS/HSM. There's a private control plane option for air-gapped installs, though that path has longer provisioning and legal steps.
[00:52] Priya: Is the KMS integration a full HSM-backed keywrap or just envelope encryption with our key?
[00:58] Lana: We support both patterns; HSM-backed keywrap is available for Private installs. For the hosted model we use envelope with customer-managed keys in supported clouds. The transcript might do "K M S" at points, sorry if the audio mislabels.
[01:14] Tomás: We're also curious about model routing — we want to offer customers both high-performance and low-cost paths. How does Redwood route between cheaper quantized variants and higher-accuracy variants?
[01:24] Samir: Smart routing is a core pattern. You define policies — latency SLOs, cost budgets, or tenant tier — and requests get routed to the appropriate model family. We also support automatic fallback to compatible variants if capacity's tight.
[01:37] Ibrahim: Ok, on capacity: BlueGate runs a managed control plane for onboarding customers to GPUs we resell. If we integrated Redwood Dedicated, can we expose a single-tenant GPU pool under our brand?
[01:49] Lana: Yes, Redwood Dedicated supports dedicated GPU pools and we can map tenancy and quotas; for channel/reseller partnerships there are options to white-label endpoints. We'll need to scope our SLAs and provisioning patterns.
[02:05] Derek: What about KV caching and prefix caching? A lot of our workloads reuse contexts and cache hits would be huge for cost. How exposed is that to the integrator?
[02:16] Lana: We expose caching knobs — automatic prefix and KV cache management. The runtime will maintain a KV cache and we can give metrics on hit rates.
[02:25] Maya: On the compliance side — SOC 2, audit logs, SSO. Our enterprise buyers need SAML and RBAC.
[02:34] Samir: We support SSO (SAML/OIDC), RBAC, audit logs, and per-token billing traces. We'll share SOC2 and our compliance packet after the call.
[02:44] Priya: Also, do you keep ephemeral logs for routing and tokens? Our policy forbids long-term retention of PII in logs.
[02:52] Lana: Retention is configurable per-tenant in Private and Dedicated; hosted customers have retention tiers. We'll document retention controls and redaction.
[03:05] Maya: Good. Let's talk pilot scope — what would you need from us to run a short benchmark and pilot?
[03:11] Lana: Representative workload: sequence length distribution, peak QPS, preferred model families, and a network topology diagram. Ideally sample prompts and latency targets.
[03:20] Ibrahim: We'll pull a traffic extract and topology. Expect to share that by Friday.
[03:25] Tomás: For the benchmark, can Redwood run both quantized 4-bit runs and fp16 so we can compare cost/latency/quality?
[03:34] Lana: Yes, we can run evals across quantization settings and provide per-token cost estimates; we'll surface quality regressions against your prompt suite.
[03:44] Derek: How do you measure quality drift? We need to avoid false negatives if quantization changes prompt outputs.
[03:50] Samir: We tie quality monitoring to prompt sets and evaluations. If a rollout causes regressions beyond a threshold we trigger alerts and can automatically rollback to a fallback model.
[03:59] Maya: Regarding network connectivity, we have some customers that forbid direct public endpoints. Can we route calls over a peered VPC or express route?
[04:08] Lana: Yes - VPC peering or private links are supported in Private and Dedicated. For hosted integrations we offer private connectivity in select regions. There's a diagram we can share.
[04:18] Ibrahim: How about cold-start latency on large models? Some of our customers care about p99 for small prompts.
[04:25] Lana: Cold-starts depend on kernel selection, quantization, and caching. We can pre-warm instances based on autoscale policies for guaranteed p99s, but that increases cost. Tradeoff decisions live in autoscale config.
[04:38] Derek: That tradeoff is the crux — customers either want lowest unit cost or strict latency SLOs. How flexible are your routing policies?
[04:46] Samir: Very flexible. You can route by tenant tier, by API key, or by request header. Also policies can be time-based for cost windows.
[04:55] Tomás: What's the onboarding timeline if we want to pilot in Q4?
[05:00] Samir: Pilot in 6-8 weeks if we get samples this week — longer if you need an on-prem Private install. Hosted pilots are fastest.
[05:10] Priya: Can we get a copy of your SOC2 and penetration test summary? Also want to review encryption at rest defaults.
[05:17] Samir: Yes, we'll attach SOC2, pentest summary, and our encryption defaults in the follow-up email.
[05:24] Maya: Pricing — we usually have variable spreads for channel-resold infra. Do you have partner pricing or channel margins?
[05:33] Samir: We have partner programs for channel/distributor arrangements; we can share a partner rate card after initial NDA. For pilots, we can also offer credits.
[05:42] Ibrahim: One more technical — GPU packing and bin-packing for small requests. Do you do continuous batching and what about latency-sensitive routing?
[05:49] Lana: Continuous batching is a core runtime optimization; we have latency-aware batching that limits batch wait time to meet SLOs while still getting batching benefits.
[06:00] (brief cross talk)
[06:08] Tomás: Any gotchas integrating into our customer portal for single sign-on and metering? We'll want to surface usage and cost per customer.
[06:15] Samir: We can provide per-tenant usage breakdowns and token-level cost; for reseller flows we can expose an API for metering to your portal.
[06:25] Maya: Cool. On the legal side, what does your standard reseller/partner agreement look like? Are there minimal revenue commitments for dedicated pools?
[06:33] Samir: Dedicated generally has reserved capacity commitments—monthly or annual. There's flexibility on commercials per partner. Legal will share templates.
[06:40] Priya: For telemetry, will you send us logs or will Redwood retain and only surface metrics? We want to own logs for audit.
[06:48] Lana: For Private we can push logs into your logging stack; for Dedicated we can set up a cross-account logging pipeline. Hosted by default keeps logs in Redwood but with export options.
[06:58] Ibrahim: Do you support GPU families other than Nvidia A-series? Some of our customers like AMD or custom accelerators.
[07:05] Lana: We primarily optimize for mainstream GPU families; we have partners evaluating other hardware but feature parity may vary. We'll be candid about performance profiles per hardware.
[07:16] Derek: Are there reference benchmarks you can share?
[07:19] Samir: Yes, we'll share our performance catalog — p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec for common model families and sequence lengths.
[07:28] Maya: Great. Let's try to scope the pilot: a single tenant customer workload, 2-week benchmark, two model variants (quant4 and fp16), and an SLO target of p95 < 350ms for small prompts. Is that reasonable?
[07:42] Lana: That sounds reasonable as a benchmark frame. We'll make a detailed plan once we see the traffic shape.
[07:50] Tomás: For the pilot instrumentation, will Redwood run canary rollouts and show us regression dashboards?
[07:57] Lana: Yes, Redwood Console has rollout metrics and quality monitoring tied to prompt sets; we can give you access to the staging console for visibility.
[08:06] (short silence)
[08:10] Samir: I want to be transparent about timelines and blockers: on-prem Private installs require legal and security review and typically 8-12 weeks plus on-site ops. Hosted pilots are usually 2-6 weeks.
[08:22] Priya: Noted. We probably start with a hosted pilot for speed, then evaluate Private for customers that require it.
[08:29] Ibrahim: Do you have a reference integration where you worked with a channel partner to white-label endpoints?
[08:36] Samir: Yes, we have a couple — we'll redact names in the case study and share patterns for white-labeling and customer routing.
[08:44] Derek: On the SLA — do you commit to end-to-end p99 on dedicated pools?
[08:50] Lana: We offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets for Dedicated with appropriate capacity reservations; exact numbers depend on config.
[08:59] Tomás: Ok let's talk commercial guardrails — would Redwood allow us to resell as a managed service with markup?
[09:07] Samir: Absolutely, channel/distributor models are supported; we just need to align on billing flows.
[09:14] (pause)
[09:18] Maya: Anything else we should cover?
[09:21] Samir: Maybe two quick technical follow-ups — Lana will run through a minimal benchmark plan and Ibrahim will share workload samples. We'll also schedule a VPC topology deep-dive.
[09:31] Lana: I'll prepare a draft benchmark spreadsheet: test scenarios, metrics to capture, and required artifacts.
[09:36] Ibrahim: We'll aim to deliver traffic extract and topology by 2026-07-30.
[09:41] Priya: I'll confirm KMS/HSM needs and any regulatory limitations by the same date.
[09:46] Samir: Great. We'll also include a whitepaper on routing/fallback and a checklist for Private installs.
[09:54] Derek: Sounds good.
[10:00] (wrap up)
[51:30] Samir: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the SE deep-dive.
[51:40] Maya: Thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
